_comment: Department of Basic Education Grade 10 Physical Sciences P1 (Physics), November 2019 national common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. The guideline is
bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. memo_answer gives the guideline's
working and final answers (tick marks removed); diagrams, graphs and circuits are described in
brackets in the question text. Data sheets printed with the paper are not transcribed.
Both PDFs were obtained from the Eastern Cape Department of Education exam archive (source_url); the
page headers read 'DBE/November 2019' and 'CAPS - Grade 10', i.e. this is the national DBE paper
FORMAT: 150 marks, 2 hours, eleven compulsory questions (Q1 multiple choice 20 marks).

subject: Physical Sciences

questions.context: QUESTION 1: MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTIONS. Various options are provided as possible answers to the following questions. Choose the answer and write only the letter (A-D) next to the question numbers (1.1 to 1.10) in the ANSWER BOOK, e.g. 1.11 E. Each question has only ONE correct answer.
questions.text: Which ONE of the following physical quantities is a scalar quantity? A A weight of 5 N B A velocity of 10 m∙s-1 east C A current of 2 A D A negative acceleration of 0,4 m∙s-2

Three forces act simultaneously on an object, as shown below. [Diagram: 3 N to the west; 5 N and 2 N to the east.] The resultant (net) force acting on the object is ... A 10 N west. B 4 N west. C 10 N east. D 4 N east.
An object accelerates uniformly when the … of the object changes with the same amount in equal time intervals. A velocity B displacement C speed D mechanical energy

The velocity-time graph for the motion of an object is shown below. [Graph: velocity rises from 0 to 2 m·s⁻¹ at 1 s, then decreases in a straight line through 0 at 2 s to -2 m·s⁻¹ at 3 s.] The object changes direction at ... A 0,5 s B 1 s C 2 s D 3 s
An object moving at speed v has a kinetic energy E. The kinetic energy now changes to ¼E. The speed of the object is now ... A ½v. B 2v. C ¼v. D 4v.
questions.topic: Mechanical energy: kinetic and potential energy

questions.text: The frequency of a wave is defined as the … A lowest point on a wave. B time taken for one complete wave. C number of complete waves per second. D number of points in phase in a wavelength.
When two wave crests overlap, the increase in amplitude is due to … A cancellation. B two waves in phase. C destructive interference. D constructive interference.
Which ONE of the following materials is a ferromagnetic material? A Chromium B Carbon C Cobalt D Calcium
The SI unit for charge is the … A ampere. B volt. C ohm. D coulomb.
The maximum work done per unit charge by a battery is the … A emf. B current. C resistance. D terminal potential difference.

questions.context: QUESTION 2 (Start on a new page.) A boy walks in an EASTERLY direction, as shown below. After he passes a tree, he continues in the same direction for another 20 m. He then stops, climbs on his skateboard and rides in a WESTERLY direction for 25 m before he finally stops. [Diagram: the boy west of a tree; the skateboarder 20 m east of the tree.] The resultant displacement of the boy when he finally stops is 10 m EAST of his initial position.
questions.text: Define the term distance.
Determine the initial position of the boy relative to the tree.
questions.memo_answer: Original position = 10 + 5 = 15 m west of the tree

questions.text: Calculate the total distance that the boy moved.
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 2.2.)
Distance = 15 + 20 + 25 = 60 m
(Accept: any answer in 2.2 + 45.)

questions.text: When the boy is on the skateboard, he skates at an average speed of 5 m∙s-1. Calculate how long, in seconds, the boy is on the skateboard during the motion.
questions.memo_answer:
v = Δx / Δt
5 = 25 / Δt
Δt = 5 s

questions.text: The total time for the motion of the boy from his initial position until he finally stops is 40 s. Calculate his average velocity.

questions.context: QUESTION 3 (Start on a new page.) An aeroplane touches down on a runway at a velocity of 67 m·s⁻¹, as illustrated below. After 30 seconds the velocity of the aeroplane is 8 m·s⁻¹. The aeroplane then continues at a CONSTANT VELOCITY for a further 800 m before leaving the runway. The length of the runway is 2 000 m.
questions.text: Define the term vector.
questions.memo_answer: A physical quantity with magnitude and direction.

questions.text: Convert 67 m∙s-1 to km∙h-1.

questions.context: 3.3 Calculate the:
questions.text: Acceleration of the aeroplane during the first 30 seconds
questions.memo_answer:
vf = vi + aΔt
8 = 67 + a(30)
a = -1,97 m·s⁻²
a = 1,97 m·s⁻² in the opposite direction

questions.text: Distance travelled by the aeroplane during the first 30 seconds
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 3.3.1.)
OPTION 1: Δx = ((vf + vi)/2)Δt = ((8 + 67)/2)(30) = 1 125 m
OPTION 2: Δx = viΔt + ½aΔt² = (67)(30) + ½(-1,97)(30)² = 1 123,5 m
OPTION 3: vf² = vi² + 2aΔx: (8)² = (67)² + 2(-1,97)Δx, Δx = 1 123,1 m
(Range: 1 123,1 m to 1 125 m)

questions.text: Time taken by the aeroplane to travel the 800 m
questions.memo_answer:
Δx = viΔt + ½aΔt²
800 = 8Δt + ½(0)Δt²
Δt = 100 s

questions.text: Length of the runway NOT USED when the aeroplane leaves the runway
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 3.3.2.)
Length = 2 000 - 800 - 1 125 = 75 m
(Accept: 2 000 - 800 - any answer in 3.3.2.)

questions.context: 3.4 Pilots should take weather conditions, such as wind and rain, into account when they calculate landing speed.
questions.text: How should a pilot adapt the landing speed if the surface of the runway is wet? Choose from INCREASES, DECREASES or REMAINS THE SAME.
Explain the answer to QUESTION 3.4.1 by referring to the stopping distance in relation to the landing speed.
questions.memo_answer: On a wet runway the tyres have less grip, and to stop within the same distance the landing speed should be less.

questions.context: QUESTION 4 (Start on a new page.) The velocity-time graph below represents the motion of a car over a time period of 12 seconds. The car initially moves NORTH. [Graph of velocity (m·s⁻¹) against time (s): A (0 s; 10 m·s⁻¹) to B (2 s; 10 m·s⁻¹) horizontal; a straight line from B down through C (6 s; 0) to D (10 s; -6 m·s⁻¹); horizontal from D to E (12 s; -6 m·s⁻¹).]
questions.text: Define the term velocity.
Describe the motion of the car from C to E.
questions.memo_answer:
From C to D: the car turns around/moves south (in the opposite direction) with a velocity that increases from 0 m·s⁻¹ to 6 m·s⁻¹, at an increasing velocity/constant acceleration.
From D to E: the car travels at a constant velocity south.

questions.context: 4.3 WITHOUT USING EQUATIONS OF MOTION, calculate the:
questions.text: Distance that the car travels from A to C
questions.memo_answer:
OPTION 1: Area A-B = L x B = 10 x 2 = 20 m; area B-C = ½bh = ½(4)(10) = 20 m; total distance = 40 m
OPTION 2: area of trapezium = ½(sum of parallel sides)h = ½(2 + 6)(10) = 40 m

questions.text: Acceleration of the car between B and C
questions.memo_answer:
a = gradient = Δv / Δt = (0 - 10) / (6 - 2) = -2,5
a = 2,5 m·s⁻² south

questions.text: How does the magnitude of the acceleration of the car between B and C compare to the magnitude of its acceleration between C and D? Choose from GREATER THAN, SMALLER THAN or EQUAL TO.
questions.memo_note: The guideline answer is SMALLER THAN, but its reason for 4.5 (the B-C slope is steeper than C-D) and the graph (2,5 m·s⁻² for B-C against 1,5 m·s⁻² for C-D) both give GREATER THAN.

questions.text: Refer to the graph and give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 4.4.
questions.memo_answer: Slope of the graph at B-C is steeper than C-D.

questions.text: Write down the direction of the resultant displacement of the car.
Use an equation of motion to calculate the instantaneous velocity of the car at t = 5 s.
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 4.3.2.)
vf = vi + aΔt
vf = 10 + (-2,5)(5)
vf = -2,5 m·s⁻¹
vf = 2,5 m·s⁻¹ north
questions.memo_note: With north positive, vf = -2,5 m·s⁻¹ points south; the guideline prints the direction as north.

questions.context: QUESTION 5 (Start on a new page.) A 2 kg ball rolls from rest from point A on a frictionless track ABCD, as shown below. The horizontal section, BC, of the track is 5 cm above the ground. The ball reaches point D, 30 cm above the ground, at a speed of 1,71 m·s⁻¹. [Diagram: track starting at height h at A, down to the horizontal section BC (5 cm above the ground), then up to D (30 cm above the ground).]
questions.text: Write down ONE term for the following statement: The sum of gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy

questions.context: 5.2 Calculate the:
questions.text: Mechanical energy of the ball at point D
questions.topic: Mechanical energy: kinetic and potential energy

questions.text: Initial height h of the ball at point A
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 5.2.1.)
Em(A) = Em(D): ½mvA² + mghA = ½mvD² + mghD
0 + (2)(9,8)h = 8,8
h = 0,45 m

questions.text: Speed of the ball while it moves between point B and point C

The 2 kg ball is now replaced with a 4 kg ball. How will the speed of the 4 kg ball compare to the speed of the 2 kg ball at point D? Choose from GREATER THAN, SMALLER THAN or EQUAL TO. Give a reason for the answer.
questions.memo_answer:
Equal to
The speed is independent of the mass of the object.
OR Speed only depends on the initial height.

questions.context: QUESTION 6 (Start on a new page.) The diagram below represents a transverse wave produced by source A. [Graph of amplitude (cm) against time (s): a wave of amplitude 50 cm with crests at 0, 8 and 16 s and troughs at 4, 12 and 20 s; d marks the horizontal distance covered by the whole drawn wave (2½ waves, 0 to 20 s).]
questions.text: Define the term amplitude of a wave.
questions.memo_answer: The maximum disturbance of a particle from its rest position.

questions.text: Write down the amplitude, in metres, of this wave.
Determine the period of this wave.

questions.context: 6.4 Calculate the:
questions.text: Speed of the wave if the wavelength is 0,8 m
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 6.3.)
f = 1 / T = 1 / 8 = 0,125 Hz
v = fλ = (0,125)(0,8)
v = 0,1 m·s⁻¹

questions.text: Distance d on the diagram
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 6.4.1.)
OPTION 1: distance = (2½)(0,8) = 2 m
OPTION 2: v = D / Δt: 0,1 = D / 20, D = 2 m

questions.context: The diagram below represents the transverse wave produced by source B. [Graph of amplitude (cm) against time (s): a wave of amplitude slightly greater than 50 cm completing 5 waves in 20 s (period 4 s).] 6.5 How does EACH of the following properties of the wave produced by source B compare to that of the wave produced by source A? Choose from GREATER THAN, SMALLER THAN or EQUAL TO.
questions.text: Amplitude
Frequency
Calculate the frequency of the wave produced by source B.
questions.memo_answer:
OPTION 1: frequency = vibrations / time = 5 / 20 = 0,25 Hz
OPTION 2: f = 1 / T = 1 / 4 = 0,25 Hz

questions.context: QUESTION 7 (Start on a new page.) A sound wave is produced by a source placed a certain distance from a building as shown below. The echo reaches the source after 8 seconds. The speed of sound in air is 340 m·s⁻¹.
questions.text: Define the term longitudinal wave.
questions.memo_answer: A wave in which the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of motion of the wave.

questions.text: Calculate the distance between the sound source and the building.
Name the property of a sound wave that influences its pitch.
Above which frequency is a sound wave classified as ultrasound?
Name ONE use of ultrasound in the medical treatment of patients.

questions.context: QUESTION 8 (Start on a new page.) The frequency and corresponding energy of electromagnetic waves are given in the table below. [WAVE | FREQUENCY (Hz) | ENERGY (J): A | 2 x 10⁹ | 1,33 x 10⁻²⁴; B | 4 x 10¹² | 2,65 x 10⁻²¹; C | 3,5 x 10¹⁵ | 2,32 x 10⁻¹⁸; D | 1,8 x 10¹⁸ | 1,19 x 10⁻¹⁵; E | f | 4,97 x 10⁻¹⁴]
questions.text: Describe how an electromagnetic wave propagates.
questions.memo_answer: An oscillating electric field in one plane produces an (oscillating) magnetic field at right angles/perpendicular to it.

questions.text: What is the relationship between frequency and energy of an electromagnetic wave, as shown in the table above?
questions.memo_answer:
The higher the frequency, the higher the energy of the wave.
OR Frequency is directly proportional to energy.

questions.context: 8.3 Calculate the:
questions.text: Frequency of wave E
questions.memo_answer:
E = hf
4,97 x 10⁻¹⁴ = 6,63 x 10⁻³⁴ f
f = 7,5 x 10¹⁹ Hz
questions.memo_note: The guideline substitution prints Planck's constant as 6,67 x 10⁻³⁴; the data sheet value 6,63 x 10⁻³⁴ J·s gives the stated answer.

questions.text: Wavelength of wave D
questions.memo_answer:
OPTION 1: c = fλ: 3 x 10⁸ = (1,8 x 10¹⁸)λ, λ = 1,67 x 10⁻¹⁰ m
OPTION 2: E = hc / λ: 1,19 x 10⁻¹⁵ = (6,63 x 10⁻³⁴)(3 x 10⁸) / λ, λ = 1,67 x 10⁻¹⁰ m

questions.text: Which wave, A or B, has the HIGHER penetrating ability? Give a reason for the answer.

questions.context: QUESTION 9 (Start on a new page.) A compass is used to determine the poles of a magnet. The compass is placed in different positions around the magnet, as shown below. The dark arrow indicates the north pole of the compass. [Diagram: bar magnet with ends X (left) and Y (right); at position 1, beside end X, the compass north points towards X; at position 2, above the middle of the magnet, the compass north points towards X.]
questions.text: Explain the term ferromagnetic materials.
questions.memo_answer: Materials that are strongly attracted by magnets and are easily magnetised.

questions.text: Is X a NORTH pole or a SOUTH pole?
At which position, 1 or 2, will the compass experience the strongest magnetic force? Give a reason for the answer.
questions.memo_answer:
(Position) 1
The magnetic field is strongest at the poles of a magnet.

questions.text: What is the direction of a magnetic field? Choose from NORTH TO SOUTH or from SOUTH TO NORTH.

questions.context: 9.5 Give ONE term for each of the following descriptions:
questions.text: The point in the Northern Hemisphere where the rotation axis of the Earth meets the surface
The point where the magnetic field lines of the Earth enters the Earth
State ONE advantage of the Earth's magnetosphere for life on Earth.
questions.memo_answer:
Protection from solar winds.
Beskerming teen sonwinde.

questions.context: QUESTION 10 (Start on a new page.) The diagram below shows two small identical spheres, P and Q, on insulated stands. The charge on sphere P is -3 x 10⁻⁶ C and the charge on sphere Q is unknown.
questions.text: Calculate the number of electrons in excess on sphere P.
questions.memo_answer:
Q = nqe
3 x 10⁻⁶ = n(1,6 x 10⁻¹⁹)
n = 1,88 x 10¹³

questions.context: The two spheres are brought into contact and are then returned to their original positions. Each sphere now carries a charge of -1 x 10⁻⁶ C.
questions.text: Calculate the original charge on sphere Q before the spheres were brought into contact.
Were electrons transferred from P TO Q or from Q TO P during contact?

questions.context: QUESTION 11 (Start on a new page.) In the circuit diagram below, the resistance of the battery, ammeter and connecting wires are negligible. [Circuit: battery with voltmeter V1 across it, switch S, resistor R, ammeter A and a parallel combination of 4 Ω and 6 Ω resistors with voltmeter V2 across it, all in series.]
questions.text: Explain the meaning of the following: A current of 5 A
questions.memo_answer: A charge of 5 C flows (past a point) in one second/per second.

questions.text: Calculate the effective resistance of the parallel resistors.
Which one of the voltmeters, V1 or V2, will show a reading if the switch is open?

questions.context: Switch S is now CLOSED.
questions.text: How does the reading on voltmeter V2 compare to that on voltmeter V1? Choose from HIGHER THAN, SMALLER THAN or EQUAL TO.
Calculate the current in the circuit if 0,3 C passes through the ammeter in 2 s.
The potential difference across resistor R is 5 V when a charge of 0,3 C flows through it. Calculate the energy transferred in resistor R.
